ca-tim-kho-chay.name: Vietnamese vegan braised eggplant
ca-tim-kho-chay.serving_basis: Four servings of eggplant braised with tofu and mushrooms for a vegetarian family meal.
ca-tim-kho-chay.description: Soft eggplant absorbs a savory-sweet tomato braising sauce with tofu and mushrooms. The edited Bếp Việt version uses plant-based seasonings throughout for an everyday vegetarian meal.
ca-tim-kho-chay.finished_dish: Eggplant is tender but still holds its shape; tofu and mushrooms are coated in a lightly glossy, tomato-rich sauce scented with leek.
ca-tim-kho-chay.excerpt: Tender eggplant, tofu and mushrooms simmered in a gently savory tomato sauce with plant-based seasonings.
ca-tim-kho-chay.serving: Serve hot in a shallow bowl with steamed rice and fresh herbs.
tips: Soak eggplant in lightly salted water for about 15 minutes, then rinse to reduce browning and bitterness.
Choose firm tofu and turn it gently so the cubes stay intact.
Check labels on soy sauce, vegan oyster sauce and seasoning powder to ensure they are plant-based.
ca-tim-kho-chay.tip: Choose firm tofu and turn it gently so the cubes stay intact.
ca-tim-kho-chay.image_alt: Vietnamese vegan braised eggplant with tofu, mushrooms and tomato in a light ceramic bowl; original Bếp Việt artwork.
preparation_steps: Wash and cut the eggplant into bite-sized pieces. Soak in lightly salted water for about 15 minutes, rinse and drain.
Cut the tofu into cubes and the mushrooms into bite-sized pieces. Sear the tofu briefly if you want it to hold its shape more firmly.
Cut the tomato, mince the garlic and slice the leek. Mix the plant-based sauces, seasoning powder, sugar and pepper with a little water.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil and sauté the white leek and garlic until fragrant. Add the tomato and cook until softened.
Add the mushrooms and tofu and turn gently, then add the eggplant and the prepared sauce with the remaining water.
Cover and simmer over low heat for about 12–15 minutes until the eggplant is tender and the sauce lightly coats the ingredients. Shake the pot occasionally instead of stirring hard.
Taste and adjust the seasoning. Finish with the green leek and fresh herbs.
ca-tim-kho-chay.time_note: Includes about 15 minutes of soaking; cooking time depends on the thickness and variety of eggplant.

editorial.variant_note: Edited by Bếp Việt from the cited reference; quantities and timing need a home-kitchen trial.

ingredients.name: Eggplant
ingredients.notes: About three medium eggplants, cut into pieces.

ingredients.name: Firm tofu
ingredients.notes: Cut into cubes; optionally sear lightly.

ingredients.name: Tomato
ingredients.notes: One medium tomato, cut into wedges.

ingredients.name: Leek
ingredients.notes: Slice the white part; cut the green part into short lengths.

ingredients.name: Vegan oyster-style sauce
ingredients.notes: Use a product clearly labeled vegan.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Use sparingly after adding soy sauce.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Add a little more if the sauce reduces before the eggplant is tender.

ca-tim-kho-chay.media_alt_text: Vietnamese vegan braised eggplant with tofu, mushrooms and tomato in a light ceramic bowl; original Bếp Việt artwork.

bun-do-buon-ma-thuot.name: Buon Ma Thuot red vermicelli soup
bun-do-buon-ma-thuot.serving_basis: Four generous bowls served as a main dish.
bun-do-buon-ma-thuot.description: Red rice vermicelli is served with freshwater crab, tomato, and pork broth in this hearty, familiar Buon Ma Thuot breakfast bowl.
bun-do-buon-ma-thuot.finished_dish: Bright orange-red rice vermicelli sits in a tomato-scented freshwater crab broth with crab cake, pork, and Vietnamese basil. The flavor is savory with gentle optional heat.
bun-do-buon-ma-thuot.serving: Blanch the noodles and divide them among bowls. Ladle over the broth, crab curds, and pork. Add Vietnamese basil, scallions, roasted peanuts, and chilli to taste; serve hot.
bun-do-buon-ma-thuot.image_alt: Buon Ma Thuot red vermicelli soup with orange-red noodles, freshwater crab, tomato, and Vietnamese basil, newly created for Bếp Việt.
bun-do-buon-ma-thuot.time_note: Estimated editorial timing; actual time depends on equipment, ingredients, and cooking experience.
tips: If using ground freshwater crab, strain it twice for a clearer broth.
Cook the crab mixture over low heat and avoid stirring so it sets into soft curds.
Use just enough annatto oil for a natural orange-red broth; no food coloring is needed.

ingredients.name: Ground freshwater crab, strained for broth

preparation_steps: Rinse the pork bones, blanch briefly, and rinse again. Mix the ground crab with about 700 ml water, gently squeeze, and strain; set the crab liquid aside.
Cut the tomatoes into wedges and finely chop the shallots. Season the ground pork with a little fish sauce, pepper, and shallot. Rinse and drain the basil and scallions.
cooking_steps: Simmer the bones with 1.1 litres of water and dried shrimp for about 25 minutes, skimming the broth. Separately heat the crab liquid over medium heat until curds rise; lift them into a bowl.

Sizzle the shallots in annatto oil, then soften the tomatoes. Add the ground pork and cook until it firms, then transfer everything to the bone broth. Pour in the strained crab liquid and bring to a gentle boil.

Season with fish sauce, sugar, and salt. Add the crab cake and heat through, then taste and turn off the heat. Blanch the noodles, divide among bowls, top with crab curds, and ladle in broth. Finish with scallions, basil, peanuts, and chilli.

keywords: Buon Ma Thuot red vermicelli soup

pho-kho-gia-lai.name: Gia Lai dry pho
pho-kho-gia-lai.serving_basis: Four servings, each with a bowl of dry pho and a separate cup of broth.
pho-kho-gia-lai.description: This Central Highlands specialty is served in two bowls: rice noodles tossed with meat and dark soy sauce, accompanied by a separate cup of clear bone broth.
pho-kho-gia-lai.finished_dish: Ivory rice noodles are topped with beef, fried shallots, bean sprouts, and basil. A separate cup of hot broth is served for sipping or pouring as desired.
pho-kho-gia-lai.serving: Divide the noodles among bowls and top with beef, bean sprouts, and basil. Toss with dark soy sauce to taste. Serve with hot broth on the side to sip or add a little at a time.
pho-kho-gia-lai.image_alt: Gia Lai dry pho with a bowl of rice noodles, beef, and herbs beside a separate cup of broth.
pho-kho-gia-lai.time_note: Estimated editorial timing; actual time depends on equipment, ingredients, and cooking experience.
tips: Blanch the rice noodles just until tender, then drain well so they do not clump.
Keep the broth at a gentle simmer rather than a rolling boil for a clean, clear flavor.
Add the dark soy sauce gradually, as brands vary in saltiness and sweetness.
preparation_steps: Rinse the beef bones, blanch for 3 minutes, and rinse clean. Halve the onion; rinse the shallots and ginger, then lightly char them until fragrant.
Chop the garlic and some shallot. Season the ground beef with a little fish sauce, pepper, and chopped shallot. Rinse and drain the bean sprouts, basil, and scallions.
cooking_steps: Simmer the beef bones with 2.2 litres of water, onion, shallot, and ginger over low heat for about 45 minutes. Skim occasionally and season lightly with salt, rock sugar, and fish sauce.
Sizzle the garlic and shallot in oil, add the ground beef, and stir until just cooked. Briefly swish the sliced beef in the hot broth, then remove it.

Blanch the noodles according to the package directions, drain, and divide among four bowls. Add the ground beef, sliced beef, sprouts, basil, scallions, and a modest amount of dark soy sauce. Ladle hot broth into four separate cups and serve alongside.

com-sen-chay-hue.name: Hue vegetarian lotus-leaf rice
aliases: Lotus-seed rice wrapped in lotus leaf
com-sen-chay-hue.serving_basis: Four vegetarian portions, served as a main or rice dish in a meat-free meal.
com-sen-chay-hue.description: Rice mixed with lotus seeds, mushrooms, and vegetables is wrapped in lotus leaf and steamed until lightly fragrant; this family-style vegetarian version is edited by Bếp Việt.
com-sen-chay-hue.finished_dish: Separate fragrant rice grains mingle with nutty lotus seeds, tofu, mushrooms, and vegetables. The lotus leaf lends a gentle aroma and a characteristic Hue presentation.
com-sen-chay-hue.serving: Carefully open the lotus leaf while hot and serve the rice in bowls or directly from the leaf. Pair with lightly spiced soy sauce and simply cooked vegetables.
com-sen-chay-hue.image_alt: Hue vegetarian lotus-leaf rice with lotus seeds, tofu, mushrooms, and vegetables wrapped in a green lotus leaf.
com-sen-chay-hue.time_note: Estimated editorial timing; actual time depends on equipment, ingredients, and cooking experience.
tips: If using dried lotus seeds, soak them for 2–3 hours and boil until tender. Fresh seeds only need the bitter core removed and a brief boil.
Let the rice cool slightly before mixing in the filling so the grains stay intact.
If the lotus leaf is torn, use two layers or steam the rice in a bowl with the leaf laid over it to retain the aroma.
preparation_steps: Rinse the rice, soak for 15 minutes, and drain. Rinse the lotus seeds and remove any bitter cores; soak dried seeds in advance and boil them until tender.
Dice the tofu, mushrooms, and carrot. Finely slice the leek. Rinse the lotus leaves and briefly dip them in hot water to soften them for wrapping.
cooking_steps: Cook the rice with water until just tender and fluffy. Boil the lotus seeds until soft but not falling apart, then drain.
Sauté the leek in oil, then stir-fry the mushrooms and carrot for 2–3 minutes. Add the tofu, peas, lotus seeds, soy sauce, salt, sugar, and pepper; gently cook until hot and fairly dry.
Fold the filling and sesame oil into the rice. Line a bowl with lotus leaf, add the rice, and wrap it closed; steam for 10–12 minutes. Unwrap at the table and serve hot with soy sauce.

keywords: Lotus-seed rice wrapped in lotus leaf

ca-tim-nuong-chay.name: Vietnamese vegetarian grilled eggplant
aliases: Vegetarian grilled eggplant with scallion oil
ca-tim-nuong-chay.serving_basis: Four side portions for a vegetarian meal.
ca-tim-nuong-chay.description: Tender grilled eggplant is dressed with leek oil and a lightly sweet-sour soy sauce for a simple Vietnamese vegetarian side that is easy to make at home.
ca-tim-nuong-chay.finished_dish: Tender, juicy eggplant with lightly charred skin absorbs fragrant scallion oil and soy dressing. Roasted peanuts add a nutty finish, making it a good match for hot rice.
ca-tim-nuong-chay.serving: Tear or cut the eggplant into bite-size pieces and spoon the soy-and-scallion dressing over it while hot. Sprinkle with peanuts and serve with rice, boiled vegetables, or braised tofu.
ca-tim-nuong-chay.image_alt: Vietnamese vegetarian grilled eggplant split lengthwise, dressed with leek and soy, and topped with roasted peanuts.
ca-tim-nuong-chay.time_note: Estimated editorial timing; actual time depends on equipment, ingredients, and cooking experience.
tips: Choose firm, glossy eggplants; grilling them whole helps keep the flesh juicy.
Grill until a chopstick passes through the flesh easily but before it turns mushy; rest for a few minutes before peeling.
Use soy sauce instead of fish sauce to keep the dish fully vegan, and adjust the chilli to taste.
preparation_steps: Rinse the eggplant, leave the stems on, and pat dry. Mince the garlic, leek, and chilli; slice the scallions and roast the peanuts if needed.
Stir the soy sauce with sugar, lime juice, and 1 tablespoon of water until dissolved. Taste for a gentle balance of salty, sweet, and sour.
cooking_steps: Grill over charcoal, roast in a 220°C oven, or air-fry at 200°C for 15–18 minutes, turning once, until lightly charred and tender.
Heat the oil and gently fry the leek and garlic until fragrant. Turn off the heat and stir in the scallions. Omit the garlic for a milder flavor if desired.
Rest the eggplant for 2 minutes, peel away any charred skin, and tear it lengthwise. Drizzle with scallion oil and soy dressing, add peanuts and chilli, and serve hot.

keywords: Vegetarian grilled eggplant with scallion oil
